cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: The paper does not define 'incoherent' preferences operationally. The final script defines it on the yes/no preference-for-recognition profile over the 18 intervals: coherent = constant, a single 0->1 switch (weakly increasing), or single-peaked (0..1..0); anything else (decreasing, U-shaped, multiple switches) is incoherent. With the attention-check exclusion (item left blank = pass) this gives 40/11/2 incoherent exclusions, matching the counts in the table notes, and 384 Berkeley participants, matching the text; Prolific gives 970 participants, 2 more than the 968 the text reports. No further exclusion rule is described in the paper, so none was added.
The BU experiment is taken to be the QM222 file only (121 completers, matching the paper's count); bu_qm221_survey_data.csv was not used.
WTP is the budgeted response (pref_rec_*_1 if the participant wanted recognition in that interval, minus pref_anom_*_1 otherwise); the hypothetical uncensored follow-ups (*_10) were not used.

For rho, the comparison-population average is the anonymous-round mean plus the Table 5 col (2) public-recognition effect (in hundreds of points), as the quantity definition specifies. c = (r1 + 2 r2 (a0 + tau)) / tau (Appendix eq. 27); gamma1 = sqrt(r1^2 - 4 r0 r2); predicted financial effect = 0.50 / c (5 cents per 10 points = $0.50 per hundred points).
cell.notes: Table 5: OLS of points on public-recognition and financial-incentive round indicators plus round-order dummies (position 1 omitted), one row per participant-round, SEs clustered by participant (fixest). Table 6 col (4): OLS of WTP ($) on interval midpoint in hundreds of points and its square, excluding the >=1700 interval, Berkeley final sample, clustered by participant. Table 7 Berkeley action-signaling parameters come from the Appendix F.1 mapping equations; a 1000-replication participant-block percentile bootstrap is printed in stdout only as a diagnostic. Attempts 1-3 were exploratory runs (data inspection and sample-definition checks); they printed no RESULT lines. No run hung; each finished in under 10 seconds.
